# PR #4875: Patch: a wrap-up that fired before the beam still leaves the AI a line when its first root move carries a surcharge, so it does not end its turn by fallback

Closes #4801

## What changed

If the host's wrap-up (R3498000) had already fired when the beam started, a surcharged first move made the decision fall back to End turn. With #97 Zephrys alone in hand, the AI passed a turn it had a play for. The wrap-up is now held off until the beam has tried every move at its root, however many nodes those moves cost. Before, it was held off for a fixed `root_branching + 1` nodes, and a 100-node Zephrys surcharge used that up inside one step. This follows the plan in the issue; the new ruling is R4801000, which amends R3498000.

- **`crates/ai/src/types.rs`**: `NodeCounter` gets a default method `end_root()` that does nothing.
- **`crates/ai/src/simulate.rs`**: the beam's slice drops its node floor. It gets a `root_tried` flag, set by `end_root`, and polls the wrap-up only once the flag is set. `create_wrap_up_counter` loses its `floor` parameter. The `capped` check and `parent.take()` are unchanged, so the hard stop (`should_stop`) is still polled before every node, root included.
- **`crates/ai/src/search.rs`**: `beam_search` calls `counter.end_root()` once its first depth has run.
- **`crates/ai/src/decide.rs`**: the new call, and an updated comment.
- **Spec**:
  - new note `spec/rulings/R4801000.md`, with its paragraph in `spec/pending/4801.md`;
  - R3498000's title notes the amendment, and an "Amended by" paragraph is added at the end, as other amended notes do;
  - one clause in §9.9 Budgets (`spec/09-architecture/9.9-practice-ai.md`);
  - one sentence in `crates/ai/README.md`, Budgets.
- With no clock, or a wrap-up that never fires, every node the counter hands out is the same as before. So the gates, fuzz, the golden replay and the server's fold of a practice claim decide exactly as they did. Only clocked hosts change: under a wrap-up the root now always finishes, within the beam's slice and the hard stop.

## Tests

All new tests are in `crates/ai/tests/ai/search.rs`, `mod r3498000_wrap_up`:
- **`r4801000_a_wrap_up_counter_is_first_polled_once_the_root_is_tried_and_the_hard_stop_still_is`**: the counter itself. The wrap-up is not polled at all before `end_root`, refuses right after it while the parent runs on, and the hard stop still stops the slice before `end_root`.
- **`r4801000_a_wrap_up_fired_before_the_beam_still_leaves_a_line_when_the_first_root_move_is_surcharged`**: the issue's reproduction, plus a check that a wrap-up that never fires decides exactly as no clock does.
- **`r4801000_a_wrap_up_fired_before_the_beam_still_tries_every_root_move_its_end_turn_last`**: the related case in the issue. Every root move gets a line, End turn included, and the beam goes no deeper than its root.
- The existing counter test now calls `end_root()` before it expects a refusal.

I checked that the new tests catch the bug: with the old 21-node floor put back temporarily, all three fail, the reproduction with the issue's exact output: `the beam was left no line: Fallback {"type":"endTurn"} after 22 nodes, stopped by Clock (no clock: {"instanceId":"c1","type":"play"})`. I then restored the code.

## Where I departed from the plan

One existing test the plan didn't mention failed: `r3696000_past_the_wrap_up_the_supply_drop_line_is_not_replied_to` in `crates/ai/tests/ai/meditative_plus.rs`, with `one beam: left 7, right 17`. It had set `root_branching` to `AI_BUDGET.nodes` only to push the old node floor out of reach, so the beam never checked the wrap-up. Under the new rule the beam checks it after its root whatever `root_branching` is.

I changed only how the test keeps the beam from stopping. It now uses plain `AI_BUDGET`. It first runs with a wrap-up that never fires (and checks that this decides exactly as no clock does) to count the checks. Then it fires the wrap-up only on the last of those checks, the search's own check before it replies to the Supply Drop line. Every outcome assertion is kept: same lines, `replied == SHORTLIST`, every world scored, stopped by the clock. The one change is that the check count is no longer `1`, since the beam now makes checks of its own.

The rejected alternative was setting `max_depth: 1` so the beam never checks; that would change the beam the test is about. I didn't consider keeping the old count of `1`, because nothing can keep it under the new rule.

## Decisions the issue left open

These are also in R4801000's "Rejected" paragraph.
- **The beam says when its root is done.** I rejected never letting the wrap-up refuse inside one step's surcharge: an auto-answer or a scored prompt in the first step would still be refused with no child, and End turn would still go untried.
- **The node floor is dropped, not kept beside the new rule.** Past a cheap root, keeping it would let the beam explore on after the host asked it to stop.
- **The counter does not count root moves.** Only the beam knows how long its root list is: kept stand-downs, walls and End turn come after `root_branching`.

## Worth a second look

- `end_root()` is called even when the first depth stopped early on budget or the hard stop. That does no harm, since `end_exploring()` comes right after and turns off the wrap-up.
- On a slow device under a fired wrap-up, the root now costs its full no-clock price; a hand Pareto Optimality is judging can cost several hundred nodes. The beam's slice and the hard stop still bound it, as the ruling's Cost paragraph says.

# #4801: Patch: a wrap-up that fired before the beam still leaves the AI a line when its first root move carries a surcharge, so it does not end its turn by fallback
Opened by @squishy-squooby.

### What happens

When the host's wrap-up (`AiOptions::wrap_up`, R3498000) has already fired by the time the beam starts, and the first root move is one `simulate` surcharges, the beam is left with no line and the decision is `Fallback endTurn`: the AI passes a turn it had plays for.

- `crates/ai/src/decide.rs:620-626` builds the beam's slice with `create_wrap_up_counter(counter, remaining - reserve, wrap_up, budget.root_branching + 1)`. The comment says the wrap-up "is first polled once the root has been expanded (root_branching and endTurn): a wrap-up that fired before the beam would otherwise leave it no line and the decision would fall back." But that floor is counted in **nodes**, not root moves.
- A surcharged step takes its extra nodes one at a time (`crates/ai/src/simulate.rs:779-783`): 100 for a play of #97 Zephrys, 40 for a lethal-size attack while a My Pawn lies in the backrow, `3 × hand` for a play Pareto Optimality judges (`surcharge_nodes`).
- So the first root `simulate` passes the floor inside its own surcharge, the counter polls `wrap_up` (`simulate.rs:171-177`), refuses, and `simulate` returns `None`. The beam reads `None` as "stop the wave" with no child yet.

Concrete: the AI holds only Zephrys at 3 mana (candidates: play Zephrys, End turn), `wrap_up` answers true, `should_stop` is unset. Result: `Fallback {"type":"endTurn"} after 22 nodes, stopped by Clock`. With no clock the same state searches 9 lines and plays Zephrys. With an ordinary card in hand the same fired wrap-up gives lines, as intended. The weakest ladder bot's floor is only 11 nodes (`root_branching` 10), so a 16-node Pareto-judged play is enough there.

### What should happen

`crates/ai/README.md`, Budgets (R3498000): the wrap-up "stops the beam's slice of the counter …: the beam's open lines end their turn and the reply and the other determinizations run on until `should_stop`". The comment at `decide.rs:620-623` states the floor exists so that a wrap-up fired before the beam never leaves it without a line. A surcharge inside the first root step should not defeat that.

### How to reproduce

Fails on `main` (3a83bd7): test `a_wrap_up_fired_before_the_beam_still_leaves_a_line_when_the_first_root_move_is_surcharged` in [`crates/ai/tests/audit_decide.rs` at bf24a52](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/bf24a52273bd5c0e7d6f9c740b28a8d7cb7f2b3e/crates/ai/tests/audit_decide.rs) (branch `claude/vigilant-mayer-pmyrhr`; `git show bf24a52:crates/ai/tests/audit_decide.rs`).

```rust
const ZEPHRYS: &str = "core-097";
fn one_card(def: &str) -> GameState {
    jackioh_cards::register_all();
    scenario(json!({
        "seed": "audit-wrap", "active": AI, "turn": 9,
        "p1": { "hand": [def], "mana": 3, "library": ["core-008", "core-011", "core-020"] },
        "p2": { "hand": ["core-011"], "field": ["core-008"], "library": ["core-008", "core-011", "core-020"] },
    })).state().clone()
}
#[test]
fn a_wrap_up_fired_before_the_beam_still_leaves_a_line_when_the_first_root_move_is_surcharged() {
    let fired = || true;
    let wrapped = |state: &GameState| {
        let mut options = AiOptions::with_budget(create_rng("audit-wrap", 0), AI_BUDGET);
        options.wrap_up = Some(&fired);
        decide(state, AI, &mut options).expect("a decision")
    };
    let plain = wrapped(&one_card("core-008"));
    assert!(plain.stats.lines > 0, "PREMISE: an ordinary root is expanded under a fired wrap-up");
    let state = one_card(ZEPHRYS);
    let unclocked = decide(&state, AI, &mut AiOptions::with_budget(create_rng("audit-decide", 0), AI_BUDGET)).expect("a decision");
    assert_eq!(unclocked.reason, DecisionReason::Search, "PREMISE: with no clock the root is searched");
    let d = wrapped(&state);
    assert!(d.stats.lines > 0,
        "the beam was left no line: {:?} {} after {} nodes, stopped by {:?} (no clock: {})",
        d.reason, action_key(&d.action), d.stats.nodes, d.stats.stopped_by, action_key(&unclocked.action));
    assert_ne!(d.reason, DecisionReason::Fallback);
}
```

Output today: `the beam was left no line: Fallback {"type":"endTurn"} after 22 nodes, stopped by Clock (no clock: {"instanceId":"c1","type":"play"})`

### Where

The AI: `crates/ai/src/decide.rs` (`plan`, the beam's wrap-up counter), `crates/ai/src/simulate.rs` (the wrap-up counter's poll and the surcharge loop).

### Version or commit

`main` at 3a83bd7.

### Notes for the fix

- Count the floor in root moves tried, not nodes: poll the wrap-up only between root expansions until the root's list is through. Or never let the wrap-up refuse inside one step's surcharge loop. Either way a wrap-up refusal inside a surcharge must not read as "stop the wave" before any child exists.
- The hard stop (`should_stop`) is not involved and must keep stopping everything.
- With no clock, or a wrap-up that never fires, a decision must stay node for node what it was (R3498000).
- A related case seen by reading only, not proven: when the root's list costs more than `root_branching + 1` nodes (kept stand-downs, auto-answers), the root's own End turn, last in the list, is never simulated under an early wrap-up. Worth a look in the same change.
- Not among the findings of the AI audit tracker #4787 (its #4791 is the budget-cut twin of this: lines left open when the slice runs out by budget).
